summary: Selected papers emphasize BMS/color-coherence jet-quenching theory, saturation analogies for QGP jet evolution, holographic hot and dense QCD phase structure, neural-network nuclear response functions, conditional diffusion for TMD inference, quantum-kernel tracking benchmarks, cross-simulator foundation-model summaries, and phase-space sampler reuse. Two caution items are included: a trigger-like quantum-ML benchmark that should not be framed as quantum advantage, and a QGP-star interpretation whose evidence is limited to weak mass-range consistency.
strongest_paper: 2608.25984 and 2608.25983: paired work connecting color coherence, BMS evolution, jet quenching, and saturation-like nonlinear dynamics in QGP jet evolution.

papers.title: Color Coherence and the Soft Structure of QCD Jets in Vacuum and the QGP
papers.abstract: Perturbative framework for soft jet evolution in vacuum and QGP using BMS evolution of Wilson-line correlators; medium effects modify boundary conditions while preserving ultraviolet structure.

papers.title: Advances in the holographic description of hot and dense QCD matter
papers.abstract: Review and extension of Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto approaches to finite-temperature and finite-density QCD-like phases including pion condensation, baryonic matter, and quarkyonic matter.

papers.title: Jet Quenching Meets Gluon Saturation
papers.authors: Paul Caucal, Kevin Eisenberg, Yacine Mehtar-Tani
papers.abstract: Applies BMS evolution and a saturation analogy to jet fragmentation in heavy-ion collisions and computes a proof-of-principle jet nuclear modification factor.

papers.title: Optimizing artificial neural networks for dipole strength predictions in light nuclei
papers.authors: Tim Egert, Weiguang Jiang, Sonia Bacca
papers.abstract: Optimized neural-network approach for electric dipole strength functions in nuclei with A < 50, with two-stage training, uncertainty-weighted losses, and high-energy regularization.

papers.title: Learning Transverse Momentum Distributions from Raw Scattering Events via Conditional Diffusion
papers.authors: Jitao Xu, Christopher Cocuzza, Kevin Braga, Daniel Lersch, Nobuo Sato, Yaohang Li
papers.abstract: Conditional diffusion model maps raw SIDIS event kinematics to TMD PDFs with uncertainty estimates in simulated CLAS12-like studies.

papers.title: Evaluating Quantum Kernel Methods for Track-Based Classification in High-Energy Physics
papers.abstract: Quantum-kernel SVM workflow for CLAS12 drift-chamber track classification scaled to large training and test sets, with ideal and noisy-simulation benchmarks.

papers.title: Cross-simulator transfer with foundation model summaries: Towards robust SKA-era reionization inference
papers.authors: Yannic Pietschke, Caroline Heneka, Ayodele Ore, Romain Meriot
papers.abstract: Self-supervised ViT summaries pretrained on cheap approximate simulations transfer to hydrodynamical simulations for calibrated simulation-based inference under realistic noise.

papers.title: Too good to go: Upcycling Phase-Space Points for Multijet Processes
papers.authors: Konrad Helms, Timo Janssen, Steffen Schumann
papers.abstract: Uses nested phase-space structure to initialize sampler adaptation for higher-multiplicity final states, demonstrated with continuous normalizing-flow samplers while preserving unbiased event weights.

papers.title: Classical and Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning for Trigger-Like Event Selection on CMS Open Data
papers.authors: Tariq Mahmood, Muhammad Awais Rafique, Talab Hussain, Juan Pablo Perez Aguilar, Alfredo Raya, Muhammad Ahsan
papers.abstract: Classical and simulated eight-qubit hybrid quantum classifiers are compared on a CMS-open-data trigger-like task; the classical ANN remains best and the study is framed as a benchmark rather than quantum advantage.

papers.title: Testing the QGP Star Hypothesis: The oMEGACat BH-2 System as a Candidate Color-Superconducting Quark-Gluon Plasma Star
papers.abstract: Argues that a mass-gap compact object could be a QGP star because its inferred mass overlaps a broad proposed QGP-star mass range.
